# DESIGN CODE NS 04

# Coco the Capybara

**US crochet terms · Intermediate · 2.5–3 hours**

A low, round, bottom-heavy capybara with a blunt sewn-on muzzle, plump stuffed
legs and a calm embroidered sleeping face. The face is embroidered, so there are
no safety eyes and no small plastic parts.

Coco stands on all four legs and measures about **10.3 cm (4 in) tall** and
**5 cm (2 in) wide**.

---

## SKILL LEVEL

Every round in this pattern is beginner-level: magic ring, single crochet,
increase and invisible decrease.

The one step that is not beginner-level is the **two-layer leg join** at Rnd 4
and Rnd 5, where you crochet a finished leg and the body together in a single
stitch. It is explained in full in technique 3, and it is worth practicing once
on a scrap magic ring before you start the body.

---

## MATERIALS

**Main yarn** — Worsted weight (#4), warm brown, about 30 g. A smooth matte yarn
shows the stitch texture best.

**Face yarn** — Worsted weight (#4), dark brown, about 5 g, for the closed eyes,
nose and mouth. Use the same weight as the main yarn; a lighter yarn changes how
the embroidery sits on the face.

**Hook** — **3.0 mm (US C-2 or D-3).** The gauge below is written for this hook.

**Eyes** — None. The sleeping face is embroidered.

**Also needed** — Polyester fiber filling, about 5–8 g; yarn needle; stitch
marker; pins. Pins matter here — the muzzle and the ears are pinned in place
before they are sewn.

> **Safety.** Coco has no safety eyes and no small plastic parts, which makes the
> face safer than a safety-eyed toy. That does not make the finished toy suitable
> for babies. Coco is a stuffed toy with a sewn-on muzzle and sewn-on ears, and
> it has not been tested to a toy-safety standard such as ASTM F963 or EN 71.
> Intended as a decorative item, or a gift for a child old enough not to chew it.
> Check the seams before giving Coco to a young child.

---

## GAUGE

Worked on a 3.0 mm hook and stuffed: **36 single crochet around measures about
52 mm in diameter.** That is 4.5 mm per stitch and 4.3 mm per round.

Check your gauge on the body after Rnd 6 rather than on a flat swatch. A stuffed
tube is the only honest test for amigurumi, and it is the measurement every
dimension in this pattern depends on.

If your 36 stitches measure wider than 52 mm, your tension is loose — crochet
more tightly, or go down a hook size. Coco at a loose gauge will show her
stuffing.

---

## FINISHED SIZE

About **10.3 cm (4 in) tall** standing on all four legs, and **5 cm (2 in) wide**
at the widest part of the body.

Coco is meant to be squat and bottom-heavy. Her legs are short relative to the
round body, and the body is one continuous curve from base to crown.

The height is the body plus the legs:

| | |
|---|---|
| Body, Rnd 1 to Rnd 20 | 20 rnd × 4.3 mm = **86 mm** |
| Front legs | 9 rnd × 4.3 mm = **38.7 mm** |
| Back legs | 8 rnd × 4.3 mm = **34.4 mm** |
| Height the legs lift the body off the table | **17 mm** |
| **Total standing height** | 86 + 17 = **103 mm ≈ 10.3 cm** |

---

## ABBREVIATIONS

| | |
|---|---|
| **MR** | magic ring |
| **ch** | chain |
| **sc** | single crochet |
| **inc** | increase — 2 sc in one stitch |
| **invdec** | invisible decrease |
| **sl st** | slip stitch |
| **st(s)** | stitch(es) |
| **Rnd(s)** | round(s) |
| **FO** | fasten off |
| **(n)** | the stitch count at the end of that round |

---

## WORKING NOTES

Work in **continuous spiral rounds**. Do not join at the end of a round and do
not chain 1 between rounds. Move a stitch marker into the first stitch of every
round — in a spiral there is no join to count from, and the marker is the only
way to know where a round ends.

Unless a note says otherwise, work every stitch through both loops.

---

## HOW IT COMES TOGETHER

The three techniques used throughout this pattern, in the order you meet them.

### 1 · The magic ring

Every piece begins with a magic ring. Pull the tail tight once the first round is
complete.

### 2 · Working in a spiral

Keep a stitch marker in the first stitch of every round. There is no seam and no
join to count from.

### 3 · The two-layer leg join

This is the only genuinely fiddly step in the pattern.

Hold a finished leg against the body, with the pinched-flat top of the leg lying
against the outside of the body. Insert your hook through **both** the leg and
the body stitch, and work one single crochet. The leg edge and the body stitch
are treated as a single stitch.

Those stitches still count as one stitch each, so every stitch count in the body
table stays correct.

Pinching the leg top flat first is what makes this easy. A round, un-pinched leg
top will not lie flat against the curved body, and the join will pucker.

---

## PART 1 — LEGS, EARS AND MUZZLE

Make these first. The legs are stuffed — plump little balls that the body rests
on.

### Leg

**Make 2 back legs (8 rounds) and 2 front legs (9 rounds).**

| RND | INSTRUCTION | STS | WHICH LEGS |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | 6 sc in MR | (6) | all four |
| R2 | [1 sc, inc] ×3 | (9) | all four |
| R3 | sc in each st around | (9) | all four |
| R4 | sc in each st around | (9) | all four |
| R5 | sc in each st around | (9) | all four |
| R6 | sc in each st around | (9) | all four |
| R7 | sc in each st around | (9) | all four |
| R8 | sc in each st around | (9) | all four — back legs finish here |
| R9 | sc in each st around | (9) | front legs only |

**Finish.** Stuff the lower half of each leg lightly, leaving the top loose.

Then **pinch the whole 9-stitch top flat into a narrow strip about 3 stitches
wide.** Press it between finger and thumb and hold it that way while you work the
join. FO with a long tail for sewing.

The back legs stop after Rnd 8 (about 34 mm). The front legs work Rnd 9 as well
(about 39 mm). The front legs are the longer pair on purpose: they join the body
one round higher up, so they need to be one round longer for all four feet to
reach the table at the same height. Make all four legs the same length and Coco
will rock back onto her haunches with her front feet in the air.

> The leg top is 9 stitches around, so a flattened edge is naturally about 5
> stitches across. Pinching it down to 3 is deliberate. The stitches you do not
> join bunch up inside the join, and that bunch is what makes the leg look plump
> rather than tubular. Do not try to keep the top flat and wide — it will not sit
> against the curved body.

### Ear — make 2

| RND | INSTRUCTION | STS |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | 6 sc in MR | (6) |
| R2 | [1 sc, inc] ×3 | (9) |
| R3 | sc in each st around | (9) |

**Finish.** FO with a long tail. Do not stuff. Each finished ear is a shallow cup
about 20 mm across and 13 mm tall.

### Muzzle — make 1

| RND | INSTRUCTION | STS |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | 6 sc in MR | (6) |
| R2 | [1 sc, inc] ×3 | (9) |
| R3 | [2 sc, inc] ×3 | (12) |
| R4 | sc in each st around | (12) |
| R5 | sc in each st around | (12) |

**Finish.** FO with a long tail. Stuff lightly, just enough to hold a dome. The
finished muzzle is about 17 mm across.

---

## PART 2 — BODY AND HEAD

Body and head are worked as one piece, bottom up. Both are 36 stitches around,
with only a shallow waist between them — that is what makes Coco read as one
continuous round blob rather than a snowman.

The legs are joined low, at Rnd 4 and Rnd 5, while the base is still curving
outward.

| RND | INSTRUCTION | STS | NOTE |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | 6 sc in MR | (6) | |
| R2 | inc in each st around | (12) | |
| R3 | [1 sc, inc] ×6 | (18) | |
| R4 | 3 sc, [1 sc, inc] ×3, 3 sc, [1 sc, inc] ×3 | (24) | join the BACK legs |
| R5 | [3 sc, inc] ×6 | (30) | join the FRONT legs |
| R6 | [4 sc, inc] ×6 | (36) | body at full width — check gauge here |
| R7 | sc in each st around | (36) | |
| R8 | sc in each st around | (36) | |
| R9 | sc in each st around | (36) | stuff the body FIRMLY |
| R10 | [7 sc, invdec] ×4 | (32) | shallow waist |
| R11 | [7 sc, inc] ×4 | (36) | head begins |
| R12 | sc in each st around | (36) | |
| R13 | sc in each st around | (36) | |
| R14 | sc in each st around | (36) | |
| R15 | sc in each st around | (36) | |
| R16 | [4 sc, invdec] ×6 | (30) | |
| R17 | [3 sc, invdec] ×6 | (24) | stuff the head firmly |
| R18 | [2 sc, invdec] ×6 | (18) | |
| R19 | [1 sc, invdec] ×6 | (12) | top up the stuffing |
| R20 | invdec ×6 | (6) | |

**Finish.** Cinch the remaining 6 stitches closed and weave the tail inside the
body.

### Joining the legs

Work Rnd 4 and Rnd 5 as the plain increase rounds printed in the table above,
but as you reach each leg position, hold a pinched-flat leg top against the body
and work the next 3 sc through both the leg and the body together (technique 3).
Those 3 sc still count as 3 stitches of the round, so the stitch counts do not
change.

**Rnd 4 — the back legs**

> Work the first **3 sc** through a leg and the body together, then **[1 sc,
> inc] ×3**.
>
> Work the next **3 sc** through the second leg and the body together, then
> **[1 sc, inc] ×3** to the end of the round.
>
> **Total 24 stitches.**

**Rnd 5 — the front legs**

> Work **7 sc**.
>
> Join a leg over the next **3 sc**.
>
> Work **10 sc**.
>
> Join a leg over the next **3 sc**.
>
> Work **7 sc** to the end of the round.
>
> **Total 30 stitches.**

The 7 – 10 – 7 spacing is what keeps Coco steady. It centers each front leg
between the two back legs, so her four feet cover the deepest footprint this
shape allows — about 65 mm across and 29 mm from front to back.

Work the numbers exactly as printed. If the front legs end up directly behind the
back legs instead of between them, Coco's footprint narrows to about 9 mm from
front to back and she will tip over forwards and backwards.

Hold the piece upside down and check that all four legs sit square before you
stuff the body.

---

## PART 3 — WHY THE LEGS JOIN SO LOW

The back legs are 8 rounds long, about 34 mm, and they join at Rnd 4 — only
17 mm above the base of the body. The front legs are 9 rounds long, about 39 mm,
and they join at Rnd 5, 21 mm up.

Different lengths, same result: **every foot hangs 17 mm below the body**, so all
four land level and the underside of the body clears the table by about that
much. Coco stands on her feet, not on her belly.

This is the single most common failure on a round-bodied animal. Legs joined at
the widest part of the body are always too high: the belly rests on the table and
the feet dangle in the air.

If Coco does not stand, check the join height before anything else.

---

## PART 4 — FACE AND ASSEMBLY

### Muzzle

Stuff the muzzle lightly and pin it to the front of the head over **Rnd 12–14**,
centered on the face. Sew all the way around with matching brown.

The muzzle should sit proud of the head, not flush with it.

Centering matters. The muzzle is about 17 mm across and the eyes go 27 mm apart,
which leaves only about 5 mm of clear face between the edge of the muzzle and
each eye. A muzzle pinned even slightly off-center will crowd one eye.

### Eyes

Embroider the eyes — do not use safety eyes.

With dark brown, work a shallow downward arc about 3 stitches wide on each side,
at **Rnd 14–15**, **6 stitches apart**, with a tiny tick angled down at each
outer end.

Six stitches keeps both eyes on the front of the face. Any wider and they wrap
around the sides. Placing them at Rnd 14–15 keeps the whole eye above the muzzle,
which is pinned over Rnd 12–14.

This closed-eye curve is what makes Coco look asleep.

### Nose and mouth

Embroider the nose and mouth **after** the muzzle is sewn on, so the stitches sit
on the finished curve rather than on a flat piece.

On the muzzle, work a small dark triangle at the top center, then a short vertical
line down from it, and a soft curved mouth to one side.

### Ears

Pinch the base of each ear so it cups forward, then sew at **Rnd 15**, about
**5 stitches apart**, angled slightly outward.

Rnd 15 is still a full 36-stitch round, so 5 stitches puts the ears on top of the
head where a capybara's ears belong. Sewing them wider apart — or onto Rnd 16,
which has already decreased to 30 stitches — pushes them out to the sides of the
head, where they disappear from the front.

### Legs

The legs were joined during Rnd 4 and Rnd 5. There is nothing to sew. Just check
that the pinched 3-stitch strip of each leg is caught fully in the round.

### Final shaping

Roll the finished piece gently between your palms to settle the stuffing into a
round, bottom-heavy shape.

---

## TROUBLESHOOTING

**Coco looks too tall** — Almost always too many plain rounds. Rnd 12–15 is the
straight section of the head, and the face is positioned on it. Adding "just one
more" round each time turns the shape into a tower and moves the face off the
round it was designed for.

**Coco will not stand** — Check the join height, not the leg spacing. The legs
belong on Rnd 4 and Rnd 5. Joined any higher, they cannot clear the underside of
the body.

**Coco tips forward or backward** — Two causes, in order of likelihood. First,
the front legs are lined up behind the back legs instead of between them: the
Rnd 5 spacing must be 7 sc, 10 sc, 7 sc. Second, Coco is deliberately narrow from
front to back, at about 29 mm, and no leg spacing changes that. If she still
tips, stuff the lower body more firmly and settle her weight back over all four
feet.

**Coco rocks back onto her haunches, front feet in the air** — All four legs are
the same length, and they cannot be. The front legs join at Rnd 5, 21 mm up, and
the back legs at Rnd 4, 17 mm up, so equal-length legs leave the back feet about
9 mm lower. Work the front legs 9 rounds and the back legs 8.

**Coco will not sit level** — Stuff the lower body firmly. A soft base lets Coco
tip forward onto her muzzle.

**The head flops back** — The waist at Rnd 10 is deliberately shallow, at 32
stitches. Do not decrease it further. A narrow neck cannot hold the head upright
on this shape.

**The muzzle looks flat** — Stuff it just enough to hold a dome.

**Stuffing shows through** — Your gauge is too loose. Thirty-six stitches should
measure 52 mm around a stuffed body. Crochet more tightly, or go down a hook
size.

**There is a small hole where a leg meets the body** — You joined a flat, wide leg
top instead of a pinched one. Flatten the whole 9-stitch top into a strip about 3
stitches wide before joining, so the stitches you are not joining bunch up inside
the join.

---

## COLORWAYS

Classic warm brown, soft grey, sandy beige, and cocoa.

---

## BEFORE YOU ASSEMBLE

Lay every component out and check it against the pattern before you sew anything:

- 4 legs — 2 back legs of 8 rounds, 2 front legs of 9 rounds
- 2 ears
- 1 muzzle
- 1 body and head, closed at the crown
